headline: Pushing Quantum Entanglement Limits
summary: Today's research explores novel frontiers in quantum entanglement, ranging from relativistic black hole horizons to engineered monitored chains and scalable trapped-ion architectures. These studies highlight both the theoretical limits of entanglement across boundaries and practical methods to scale fault-tolerant hardware.

themes.title: Black Hole Entanglement and Gravitational Dynamics
themes.body: Investigation into how freely falling spatial superpositions can generate entanglement from scratch across an event horizon, revealing insights into soft-graviton bremsstrahlung and transverse teleportation.

themes.title: Monitored Quantum Chains and Scaling
themes.body: Analysis of the effective Hamiltonians in monitored Majorana chains, showing how correlated power-law hoppings drive unconventional log-squared system size entanglement scaling.

themes.title: Scalable Ion Crystal Architectures
themes.body: Proposing frequency-multiplexed parallel gates for quantum LDPC codes on a two-dimensional ion crystal, achieving low logical error rates through adiabatic error suppression.

connections.body: Both theoretical works explore unconventional entanglement properties and scaling limits, moving beyond standard bipartite entanglement paradigms.
